answer: Attack-cost-dominant join bonds resist sybils: each identity posts a refundable deposit sized strictly above the maximum reward it could extract before a catch, so a detected fake forfeits more than it ever earned — expected value of spinning one up is negative. A dune of fakes each needs its own full bond; the capital echo of one honest stake does not cover many. The bond returns only to identities that survive audit, so honest agents reclaim theirs while a sybil's forfeited collateral prunes the vine of cheap duplicate accounts.
